comment: Our review engine on AACR-Bench, the corpus a direct competitor published.
**Why this corpus**: 200 real PRs, 10 languages, 1,505 expert-confirmed issues and **three context levels, the
third of which is Repo Level** - so **it measures cross-file behaviour, which is our distinctive claim**.
**And the caveat that belongs in the artifact**: **Alibaba built both the tool and the benchmark it wins on**,
and an independent party said so - *"an instrument that agrees with itself is not evidence."* **Their reported
absolute precision is 33.9%**, so **their 33.90-versus-7.23 gap and their 9x token claim are their measurements
on their corpus, not runs reproduced here.**
route: our engine reading each PR diff; no bot account installed
comparisonBasis: their published figures, not a run we performed

scoring.protocol: one judge verdict per (finding, golden) pair, then a maximum bipartite matching per pull request; the same protocol for both reviewers in the same job
scoring.emissionRule: actionability gate: the range covers an added line AND (the suggestion names an action OR the finding quotes added code)

arms.file: one call per file per lane, at most 3 findings per file per lane
arms.pullRequest: one call per lane for the whole pull request, at most 16 findings for the pull request

scoring.registeredRule: the pull-request arm at 16 findings per pull request exceeds the competitor figure of 0.4500 F1 on the same corpus, same judge, same goldens; the file arm stays in the same job as the control
scoring.changedFrom: the previous protocol consumed each golden with the first finding that matched it, in judging order

pullRequestArm.view: one call per lane over the whole pull request, one budget for the pull request

armsPairedTest.view: pull-request arm vs file arm, same pull requests, same goldens, same judge
